Subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler bake-off — post-call recap & proposed next steps

Hi John —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery + the items we agreed on during the call:

- Goal: validate inference latency, cost-per-token, and quality on Acme's typical prompt set (customer support and summarization).
- Competitors in scope: Hyperscaler A (managed LLM endpoints), Hyperscaler B (AI service), and Redwood Dedicated.
- Success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 350ms for 512-token prompt, cost delta <= 20% vs your baseline, and semantic quality parity within 5% on rouge/accuracy evals.
- Owner: Redwood will deliver a bake-off test plan and runtime configs; Acme will share the anonymized prompt set and an initial 500 example prompts.
- Timeline: kickoff next week, 2-week test window, final results & recap in week 3.

I've attached a first-pass test plan (redwood-bakeoff-test-plan-v1.xlsx) and a short SLA proposal. Action items:
1) John — share the prompt set and confirm whether we should include your in-house quantized model in the test matrix (by EOD Friday).
2) Marissa/Aditya — finalize the test configs and capacity reservations for the Dedicated runs.
3) Vanessa — prepare a short evaluation harness (script + metrics) and repo link.

Can we lock the kickoff for Tuesday 7/7 at 10am PT? If that doesn't work, propose 7/8.

Thanks,
Marissa

--

John — good question on baseline. We should absolutely compare to your current Hyperscaler spend (your procurement numbers) for the cost delta metric. From Redwood's side we'll report both: 1) cost-per-token (absolute) and 2) % delta vs your reported baseline. That way your finance team can see the direct comparison.

Also attaching a short note on the test matrix and what we'll measure:
- Latency: p50/p90/p95 for 128/512 token prompts.
- Cost: end-to-end cost per 1k tokens for each provider, including expected egress and model variant pricing.
- Quality: automated semantic similarity (embedding-based), rouge for summarization tasks, and a small manual QA pass (10 hand-labeled examples) for edge-case fidelity.

Aditya — can you confirm the Dedicated capacity we can reserve 7/7–7/20 and the VM/kernel configs for Hyperscaler parity runs? Vanessa — if you can share the eval harness repo link I can add it to the Drive doc.

Thanks,
Marissa

Looping in capacity details. Marissa — we can reserve a Dedicated pool from 2026-07-07 through 2026-07-20 with the following suggested configs to match Hyperscaler parity:
- Instances: 4x A100-equivalent GPU nodes (continuous batching enabled)
- Sequence length cap: 1024 tokens
- Quantization: int8 run for cost parity, and fp16 run for quality comparison
- Batching: target batch latency 50ms, adaptive throttling for p95 control

I'll provision the pool once Acme shares the prompt set and we get final sign-off. Vanessa — I'll need the eval harness repo to wire up the metrics exporters.

Thanks,
Aditya
